as a reference, here is my answer for those wanting to know it.

in modern english we often have the terms XXXXX and XXXXXe for the same thing. the terms are only distinct because of the addition of the -e suffix.

a:

this could be called "accidental" and is related to the suffix -e ("from -").
in modern english, the two terms are usually used interchangeably, and that's a fairly simple thing to correct (in fact, i have done so myself, often by just changing the name to something completely unrelated, as my first name is already a noun phrase).
